questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It's not our book; it must be theres .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It's not our book; it must be theres.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Theirs.

Key Points

  • The possessive pronouns include 'yours, your, my, mine, our, ours, its, his, her, hers, their, theirs '. These are all words that demonstrate ownership.
  • Theirs is a possessive pronoun.
  • So, the correct answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  •  The idea that theirs needs an apostrophe comes out of the fact that every other word with, ‘s indicates possession, so English speakers sometimes think theirs should be spelled their’s. However, this is always incorrect –               theirs is the only correct spelling.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India have increased 50 times over the last three years.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

A Study has shown that the use of mobile data in India have increased 50 times over the last three years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2), i.e., Has increased 50 times.

Let's look at the following points-

  •  The sentence uses the incorrect plural verb 'have increased'.
  •  The subject of the verb is the singular 'use'.
  •  Important Point: 
  •  Subject Verb Agreement Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb; while a plural subject requires a plural verb. Example: She talks. (Singular); They talk. (Plural).
  •  Here, the singular subject 'Use' requires the singular present perfect verb 'Has increased'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence. Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, contributing to sustainable population growth and a healthier society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. promoting a viable population increase .

Key Points

  • The given sentence emphasizes the role of family planning programs in sustainable population growth.
  • Option 1, "promoting a viable population increase," maintains the idea of sustainability and growth, which aligns with the original meaning.
  • Options 2, 3, and 4 introduce negativity or excessiveness (discouraging, explosion, unbalanced growth) that is not intended in the original context.

Correct sentence: Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, contributing to promoting a viable population increase and a healthier society.

Additional Information

  • Ensuring a viable population increase implies growth that is manageable and beneficial to the society in the long term.

Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution required.

I sometimes pass a delivery man wheeling a large handcart of Japanese food. The card bears a striking message:

‘Creating a world where everyone believes in his own authenticity.’

options.text: Been created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity

options.html: Creating a world whereas everyone believes in their own authenticity

The correct answer is "No Substitution Required". 

Key Points

  • The underlined segment correctly uses the present participle "Creating" to indicate an ongoing process or aim, which aligns with the message intended to convey an aspiration or vision.
  • The use of "everyone" followed by "in his own authenticity" is traditionally correct but may not align with contemporary preferences for gender-neutral language.
  • However, the focus of this question is on the clause structure rather than pronoun choice.
  • Option 1 ("Been created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity") alters the tense inappropriately and lacks the auxiliary verb necessary for the passive voice, rendering it grammatically incorrect.
  • Option 2 ("Created a world where everyone believes in their own authenticity") changes the tense and removes the aspect of ongoing action or aspiration, which alters the intended meaning of the sentence.
  • Option 3 ("Creating a world whereas everyone believes in their own authenticity") introduces "whereas," which is incorrect because "whereas" is typically used to contrast two statements, not to introduce the content of a vision or goal.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’ The forecast predicts that there will be little rain in the month of July.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’

The forecast predicts that there will be little rain in the month of July.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- No substitution required​.

Key Points​​

  • ​Let's look at the difference between the following adjectives:
    • little- hardly any. (used in a negative sense)
    • a little- some but not much.
    • the little- not much but all that is available.
  • All of these adjectives are used with uncountable nouns.
  • Whereas the adjectives 'few' and 'many' are used with plural countable nouns.
  • As 'rain' is an uncountable noun, 'little' will be used in the underlined part of the sentence.
  • The modal verb 'must' is inappropriate as a prediction may be true or false.
  • Thus the 4th option will be the correct choice.
     

​Correct Sentence: The forecast predicts that there will be little rain in the month of July.

 ​​​​Additional Information  ​​

  • ​​Let's look at the difference between the following adjectives:
    • few- hardly any. (used in a negative sense)
    • a few- some but not many.
    • the few- not many but all that is available.
  • All of these adjectives are used with plural countable nouns.

questions.question: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. People in the remote village of Kerela are now totally self sufﬁcient and liberal and no longer (waited) till people from urban areas dish out empowerment as a special privilege or favor.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

People in the remote village of Kerela are now totally self sufﬁcient and liberal and no longer (waited) till people from urban areas dish out empowerment as a special privilege or favor.
questions.solution:
Correct option - 1

Since, the main verb are which is used in the sentence is a present form. Hence, same tense should be followed through out the whole sentence i.e. simple present tense. Thus, options 2 & 4 are eliminated. Also, people is a plural noun. So, according to sub-verb agreement, verb should also be plural. Thus, option 3 is eliminated.Hence, replace waited with wait. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - People in the remote village of Kerela are now totally self sufﬁcient and liberal and no longer wait till people from urban areas dish out empowerment as a special privilege or favor.

questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

He complained of (having harassed) by the court of law.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'having been harassed'

Key Points

The given bracketed part to be replaced with 'having been harassed' 

  • According to grammar, we use the passive voice when the doer of the verb is somebody else. In the given sentence, the verb 'harassed' has a doer which is not mentioned. So we need to use passive voice.

So the correct sentence is- He complained of having been harassed by the court of law.

questions.question: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. They have a distinct focus on (beautifying leadership) through Innovation, and Social Responsibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

They have a distinct focus on (beautifying leadership) through Innovation, and Social Responsibility.
questions.solution:
Correct option - 2

Firstly, focus is done on people who want to improve their leadership skills through putting new things in use and acting responsibly in the society. 

Now, let's check the meaning of adjectives used in the options :-

Decorating - To make something more attractive by adding things to it.

Grooming - To prepare for a position, election, etc.

Illuminating - Giving light; informative; to make brighter and more visible.

Beautifying - To make something beautiful that brings pleasure.

With reference to the context, leadership which is an inner skills and characteristics is being focused. Because, grooming their leadership skills will help them achieving their goal. Options 1, 3 & 4 are focusing on a thing or person from outer side. The word grooming leadership can be an appropriate word for improving the bracket. So, option 2 i.e. grooming leadership is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - They have a distinct focus on grooming leadership through Innovation, and Social Responsibility.

questions.question: Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4. Ruby does not like (me coming so late).
questions.questionHtml:
Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.

Ruby does not like (me coming so late).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "my coming so late".

Key Points

  •  ‘I’ is a subject pronoun and its usage will be incorrect in the given sentence.

  • In the given question the gerund 'coming' is used as a noun.

  • Hence it will take a possessive pronoun "my" before it.

  • Therefore option 2 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence: Ruby does not like my coming so late.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. MS Dhoni has no immediate plans to retire.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

MS Dhoni has no immediate plans to retire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. No improvement.

Key Points

  • 'Immediate plans' indicates a present tense
  • so the present tense singular auxiliary 'has' is used appropriately.
  • The infinitive form of the verb 'retire' is used here with 'to' preceding it, which is correct.
  • The infinitive form of a verb is usually preceded by to (e.g., to run, to dance, to think). Thus the sentence doesn't need any improvement.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mr. Adhil called back but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Mr. Adhil called back but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed.

options.text: called down but he wasn’t able to
options.html: called down but he wasn’t able to

options.text: called off but he wasn’t able to
options.html: called off but he wasn’t able to

options.text: called around but he wasn’t able to
options.html: called around but he wasn’t able to

options.text: called up to but he wasn’t able to
options.html: called up to but he wasn’t able to

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "called around" means to make a series of phone calls to different places or people in order to find or obtain something.
  • This phrase fits the context, as Mr. Adhil was trying to find a scooter part and likely made multiple calls to do so.
Therefore, the correct substitution is called around but he wasn’t able to.
 
Correct Sentence: "Mr. Adhil called around but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "called down but he wasn’t able to" – "Called down" is not appropriate in this context.
  • Option 2: "called off but he wasn’t able to" – "Called off" means to cancel, which does not fit the context.
  • Option 4: "called up to but he wasn’t able to" – "Called up to" is not idiomatic or appropriate here.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. You are welcome to partake this light refreshment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

You are welcome to partake this light refreshment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'to partake of'.

Key Points

  • The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'to partake of' should be used instead of 'to partake'.
  • The phrase ‘partake of’ means to experience something along with others or to have a portion.
    • Example: The feast is ready, but no one has come to partake of it. 
  • The given sentence states that you are welcome to have a portion of this light refreshment
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: You are welcome to partake of this light refreshment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. While driving down, Girish having to apply. for official permission to cross the two states.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

While driving down, Girish having to apply. for official permission to cross the two states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "had to"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the usage of "having to" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "had to".
  • "having" is a gerund or present participle we don't have to use it we need a modal verb i.e. "had to" it is used for moral obligatory.
  • Let's see an example-
    • Did she have to pay a fine?

Hence, the correct sentence is- While driving down, Girish had to apply. for official permission to cross the two states.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required.' The government has ordered that all illegal structures around heritage buildings must be brought down.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required.'

The government has ordered that all illegal structures around heritage buildings must be brought down.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'No substitution required' 

Key Points

  • The sentence suggests that there are constructions surrounding heritage buildings that have developed without authorized permission and the Government has ordered to demolish those constructions to protect the antique buildings.
  • The sentence requires a preposition that will indicate illegal structures ‘surrounding’ or ‘situated on every side ‘of heritage buildings.
  • Hence the preposition ‘around’ which means ‘surrounding’ or ‘encircling’ is correctly used in the given sentence.

Additional Information 

  • ‘Without’ is a preposition that means not having something.
  • ‘Towards’ is a preposition that means in the direction of someone or something.
  • ‘Into’  is a preposition that indicates something inside.
  • Hence all these are inappropriate in the given context and the sentence requires no substitution.

questions.question: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. The attention has shifts to make crops 'climate-proof".
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The attention has shifts to make crops 'climate-proof".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb form "shifts".
  • The sentence suggests an action that has already happened, so the correct verb form should be "shifted."
  • The correct phrase should be "The attention has shifted to make crops climate-proof."
  • Thus, the error is located in the verb form.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "The attention has shifted to make crops 'climate-proof'."
 
Additional Information
  • No improvement – This option would be correct if the sentence were already grammatically correct, but it is not.
  • Shift too – This option is grammatically incorrect and does not fit the context of the sentence.
  • Shifting to – This option is incorrect because the sentence implies that the action has already been completed.
